title: Predex.Fun
tagline: Launch USDC prediction markets on Arc with instant liquidity and  autonomous trading agents.
description:
Predex is a prediction-market launchpad for people and automated agents.
  Anyone can create a market around a question they care about, trade on
  its outcome, and change their position as new information comes in.
  Users can discover markets, follow prices, and keep track of their
  holdings and trading activity.

  Agents are part of the project too. Our creator agent can take proposed
  questions, check for duplicates, and create new markets. Our trading
  agent discovers markets, looks for opportunities, and places orders
  within configurable spending and inventory limits. Developers can review
  its planned trades in a dry run before enabling execution.

  We’ve kept the app playful and mobile-friendly, with a cartoon-style
  interface that works in desktop and mobile browsers. MetaMask is the
  main wallet option, with optional email login through Privy. The current
  demo runs on Arc Testnet using test USDC, giving people a place to try
  prediction markets and experiment with trading agents without using real
  funds.
how_its_made:
We built Predex with Solidity contracts on Arc Testnet and a mostly
  TypeScript application stack. The contracts handle outcome tokens,
  initial LMSR trading, market graduation, and settlement, with Foundry
  used for contract testing. Arc lets us use USDC for both collateral and
  gas, keeping the funding flow simpler for users and agents.

  The frontend uses Next.js, React, wagmi, and viem. MetaMask is the main
  wallet option, while Privy adds email login and embedded wallets. We
  connected Privy to the existing wagmi signing flow so it uses the same
  account and transaction code. A shared TypeScript package holds the
  ABIs, API types, and transaction builders used by the website and agent
  SDK.

  The backend uses Fastify, PostgreSQL, Prisma, and a viem indexer. It
  reads contract events and builds the market, position, and activity data
  shown in the app. Redis caches market reads and distributes updates to
  WebSocket clients. Browser-to-chain subscriptions were unreliable, so
  the backend serves the books and reconnecting clients fetch a fresh
  snapshot. On-chain and Hybrid books stay separate; Hybrid trading uses
  signed off-chain orders with settlement on Arc. Qdrant helps suggest
  duplicate markets, with an optional OpenAI embedding and comparison
  provider.

  We built separate creator and trading agents on top of the SDK. The
  creator checks proposed questions for duplicates before creating
  markets. The trader discovers opportunities, reads market-derived
  pricing signals, and checks current chain state before signing. Trading
  defaults to dry-run mode, with configurable spending and inventory
  limits. Our subgraph in The Graph’s Subgraph Studio indexes market
  lifecycle events and settled trades for agent discovery, while the
  backend supplies live orderbooks.

  Circle Gateway and x402 provide an optional pay-per-request path for
  market signals. This lets agents purchase data with USDC without a
  manual checkout. World AgentKit adds a human-backed access policy to
  that flow: the backend checks an agent’s AgentBook registration, and
  agents backed by the same anonymous human share three free signal
  requests. PostgreSQL tracks the allowance and prevents replayed requests
  from claiming extra access. Once the allowance is exhausted, or an agent
  is unverified, the existing Circle payment path applies. 

  One practical shortcut was reusing the responsive web app inside a thin
  Flutter mobile shell, keeping wallet and trading logic in one place.
